C0.quote: a committee is to be set up each year to select
C0.note: Aggregation of agents' single-peaked preferences into a collective choice via social choice rules and mechanisms.

C1.quote: I then identify necessary and sufficient conditions for social choice rules
C1.note: Main results characterise SCRs implementable in mixed information equilibria, an incentive property combining Nash and dominant-strategy implementation. AX and SB fit almost equally; SB chosen as primary because implementability is the central property.

C2.1.value: state / message profile (reported alignment and preference); "reported peaks"
C2.1.quote: assigns an outcome to each message profile

C2.2.quote: P is the set of all strict, complete and transitive alignments over X
C2.2.note: Messages contain a reported alignment, a reported strict single-peaked preference and an arbitrary component Li. The OTH component is the alignment report plus extra message components such as integers and alternatives.

C2.3.quote: The preferences of agents are private knowledge

C2.4.quote: ensures nobody has an incentive to unilaterally misreport the common ordering
C2.4.note: States (held) and messages (submitted) have separate notation.

C3.1.quote: ensures that the private preferences are also reported truthfully
C3.1.note: All results concern implementability, which considers misreports.

C4.1.note: No utility, welfare, satisfaction, cost or distortion notions are used for voters.

C5.1.note: Criteria used are strategy-proofness, unanimity, anonymity and no veto power.

VOT.quote_behav: ensures nobody has an incentive to unilaterally misreport the common ordering
VOT.quote_info: this alignment is common knowledge amongst the agents
VOT.note: Agents know the common alignment but not others' preferences.

DES.quote_behav: she can identify which SCR she should choose
DES.quote_info: the designer is uncertain about the underlying alignment
DES.note: Designer chooses a mechanism or SCR robust to uncertainty. Her information is the set A of possible alignments.

C7.1.note: Both voters and designer are treated as optimising.

C8.1.quote: a relevant solution concept called implementation in mixed information equilibria
C8.1.note: OTH = implementation in mixed information equilibria: Nash in the public state, dominant strategies in the private state.

C8.2.quote: implements a social choice rule f in mixed information equilibria
